messages:
Emma (Support): customer ACME (acct_987) says invoice INV-20260310-ACME shows ~24k embed units but dashboard ~12k. they think we're double-charging for rerank embeddings. filing here to triage.

Ryan (Billing): can you paste invoice id + billing window and a small sample of the usage CSV? i'll pull the bill lines.

Emma (Support): INV-20260310-ACME, window 2026-03-10 00:00 -> 2026-03-11 00:00 UTC. CSV excerpt:
```
timestamp,product,units,meta
2026-03-10T02:12:04Z,embeddings,24000,model=rerank-v1;customer=acct_987
2026-03-10T02:12:05Z,embeddings,12000,model=rerank-v1;customer=acct_987
```
(so two lines, one at 24k and 12k during same window — weird).

Olivia (ML Eng): quick q: are they using pairwise=true on rerank? if pairwise is enabled we expand pairs which should be billed as pairwise vectors, but we have a rule to bill either per-input or per-pair depending on the API flag. also: any batching or truncation in the request?

Emma (Support): customer attached request sample (sanitized):
```json
{"model":"rerank-v1","pairwise":true,"inputs":["short text A","short text B"],"batch_size":4,"truncate_to":256}
```

Dev-Bot: metering.event.rerank logged: {items_count: 8, pairwise: true, batches: 2, padded: true, truncation_applied: true} (ingest id: evt_8f3a).

Olivia (ML Eng): hypothesis: when pairwise=true + batching>1 + padding/truncation, our meter was expanding pairs per-batch chunk instead of deduplicating across the full request. that can double-count pairs if the client split inputs and we re-pad per-chunk.

Ryan (Billing): that would explain the ~2x. can you repro and produce a delta (units billed vs expected)? need that to calculate credit.

Olivia (ML Eng): repro steps i used locally:
1) send 2 inputs with pairwise=true in a client that sets batch_size=4 (client-side chunking)
2) server splits into two sub-batches, pads to 4, expands pairs inside each chunk -> results in 8 vectors measured
3) expected behavior: expand pairs across original input set -> 2 pairs -> 2 vectors.
Repro curl (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ***" \
  -d '{"model":"rerank-v1","pairwise":true,"inputs":["A","B"],"batch_size":4}'
```
I ran with metering debug, got meter_count=8, expected_meter_count=2.

Emma (Support): pinging @ryan billing: delta ~= 16k units for that invoice (24k charged vs 8k expected when you sum other lines). rough math: 2x on ranges where pairwise+batch occurred.

Ryan (Billing): ok. i'll compute exact credit. should we just apply full refund for overcharged units and notify ACME? please also attach a short blameless root-cause note.

Olivia (ML Eng): created PR to fix meter: ensure pair expansion runs on the canonical input list pre-chunk and mark pair tuples with canonical ids to dedupe across batch boundaries. also added unit tests for padding+batching combos. PR: https://git.redwood.internal/p/r/4583 (internal). change landed on branch and staged in canary.

Dev-Bot: deploy-canary succeeded for metering service at 2026-03-12T11:22:03Z (deploy id dep_774).

Emma (Support): Ryan — we've calculated the credit: invoice INV-20260310-ACME overcharged by 16,000 embedding units -> credit $80. (customer on metered pricing $0.005/unit). i've queued a credit and emailed ACME with explanation + link to support thread.

Ryan (Billing): credit processed and posted to invoice, sent follow-up to ACME. left internal note about monitoring similar accounts for same pattern.

Olivia (ML Eng): added monitoring alert rule to detect large ratio (charged_units / dashboard_units > 1.5) for rerank endpoints (rule id mon-rr-21). will roll to prod after canary validation.

Emma (Support): customer acknowledged and said refund + explanation fine. marking resolved. :white_check_mark:

Ryan (Billing): closing on our side too.

Olivia (ML Eng): leaving postmortem stub in #postmortems, will link to PR + metrics.

Emma (Support): thanks all — good catch.
